sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Delaware, Ohio?
sections.html:
Whether a Delaware owner hires an agent, goes it alone, or deals with a cash buyer, the deed ends up with the Delaware County Auditor and Recorder. The city is the county seat, set on the Olentangy River along U.S. Route 23 north of Columbus. Growth has been fast: the Census Bureau puts July 2025 at 46,636 people, 12.9 percent above its 2020 base of 41,297.

The city's own fast-facts page says Delaware draws people looking for affordability, lower income taxes, good schools and small town living. It also says the population has almost doubled since 2000.

sections.h2: Why does Delaware's history show up in its housing?
sections.html:
Delaware is an older town, and the oldest streets sit around downtown and the university. The city was built on the site of a Mingo village called Pluggy's Town, and the town plan was filed in 1808. In 1812, Delaware lost the vote to become Ohio's capital by a single vote to Columbus.

Railroads arrived in 1851, and Ohio Wesleyan University was founded in 1844. The university still anchors downtown along South Sandusky Street, and the city says its downtown is 94 percent occupied.

sections.h2: How do Delaware's homeowner statistics read?
sections.html:
Census Bureau QuickFacts for 2020 through 2024 describe Delaware this way:

  • Owner-occupied homes carry a median value of $318,400, and 64.7 percent of the 16,728 households own.
  • Households average 2.57 people; renters pay a median gross rent of $1,286.
  • Owners with a mortgage have median monthly costs of $1,892.
  • Median household income is $99,786, and 47.8 percent of adults 25 and over hold at least a bachelor's degree.
  • Workers spend 25.6 minutes getting to work on average.
  • Residents under 18 make up 23.8 percent, and those 65 and older 14.7 percent.

sections.h2: Which public schools cover a Delaware address?
sections.html:
Three public districts reach into the city, so one block can differ from the next. The city's fast-facts page sizes each one.

Public school districts within Delaware city limits (source: City of Delaware fast facts)
DistrictApproximate studentsCity's description
Delaware City School DistrictAbout 6,000The historic city district
Olentangy Local School DistrictOver 24,000Covers a large area across several jurisdictions
Buckeye Valley School DistrictAround 2,300Smaller district reaching the city

The Delaware City district's high school is Rutherford B. Hayes High School, and its middle school is John C. Dempsey Middle School. Check the parcel before a listing names a district.

sections.h2: What roads and employers tie Delaware to the region?
sections.html:
U.S. Routes 23, 36 and 42 pass through the city, and Ohio Route 37 crosses it east to west. The Delaware Municipal Airport lies southwest of the central business district.

The city says no single sector dominates its economy. Its top employers include Kroger grocery and distribution at about 2,496 jobs, Ohio Wesleyan University at 1,571, Delaware County government at 1,114, OhioHealth at 1,022 and Delaware City Schools at 996. The list also includes automotive parts distribution, manufacturing and health care. The same page says many local graduates rent for a time and buy once they have families.

sections.h2: What do parks and downtown add to a Delaware listing?
sections.html:
The city lists three larger community parks, a public swimming pool, miles of trails, an executive golf course, two free splash pads and an urban forest of more than 18,000 trees. The Delaware Community Center YMCA is another named amenity. Downtown has about 310,000 square feet of ground-floor commercial space, around 60 percent of it retail, restaurant and entertainment use.

Those are concrete points to put in a listing. The city also reports bronze-level SolSmart status from 2022, a small solar array at its public works facility and a conversion of streetlights to LED.

sections.h2: Which city permit and property rules touch a Delaware sale?
sections.html:
One city department handles zoning, property maintenance and building review, and its building division is state-certified. Its FAQ answers several questions a seller or buyer will hit.

  • Structural, electrical or mechanical work likely needs a permit; so do fences, decks, sheds, garages and additions. Patios do not.
  • Property line disputes are a civil matter between neighbors; the city suggests having the parcel surveyed.
  • Starting in 2026, contractors no longer need to register with the city.
  • All vehicles, including trailers, must be parked on a hard surface such as asphalt, concrete or existing gravel; new or expanded gravel parking is not allowed.
  • Signs in the right-of-way, tree lawns and on utility poles are prohibited and are removed by code enforcement.

Formal violation notices are posted on the property, and a vacant property's notice is mailed to the owner of record with the county auditor. When a deadline passes, the city may make the fix and invoice the owner, and unpaid invoices can turn into a lien or ride on the tax bill. Charges through the city prosecutor are also possible. Clear any notice before listing, because a lien shows up in a title search.

sections.h2: What do the Delaware County offices handle on valuation, deeds and recording?
sections.html:
The Delaware County Auditor's page on the 2026 triennial update says the informal review period is over. A formal complaint about a valuation goes to the Board of Revision, with filing open from January 1, 2027, through March 31, 2027, on the form listed with the Auditor's other forms. That page also carries the Real Property Conveyance Fee Statement, DTE 100, and the Auditor's office can quote the conveyance fee rate for your sale.

Recording follows. The Recorder's fee page shows $39 for a deed's first two pages, a figure that includes a $5 preservation surcharge, plus $8 for every added page. The office sits at 145 N. Union Street and accepts documents until 4:00 p.m. on weekdays, with recordings handled between 8:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. Rates on a county page can change, so call before mailing a check.

sections.h2: What does the state require a Delaware seller to disclose?
sections.html:
Under R.C. 5302.30, an owner of a home with up to four units must complete the Ohio disclosure form and give the buyer a signed copy. A buyer who sees the form, or a later amendment, only after signing may cancel in writing within three business days, as long as that happens before the earlier of thirty days from acceptance and closing.

The rule reaches sales, land installment contracts, lease-options and exchanges. Heirs who have not lived in an inherited house for a year are excluded, and so are transfers between spouses or to direct-line relatives.

sections.h2: When does a cash purchase help a Delaware owner?
sections.html:
A cash purchase helps when time or condition outweighs the last dollar of price. Deferred repairs, a code notice, sitting tenants or an unsettled estate can slow a listing. A buyer taking the house as it is removes showings and repair haggling.

Weigh any figure against a listed sale after repairs, the months of carrying costs, and the property tax still accruing. Keep each buyer's written price, closing date and cost split side by side.

faqs.q: What is the window to contest a Delaware County valuation?
faqs.a: The 2026 triennial update's informal review has closed. The Auditor lists a formal complaint to the Board of Revision as open from January 1, 2027, to March 31, 2027, using the Auditor's own form.

faqs.q: Which home projects need a Delaware permit?
faqs.a: Fences, decks, sheds, garages and home additions need permits, and so does any structural, electrical or mechanical work. Patios do not. Ask the Building Division what is needed to close an unpermitted structure before listing.

faqs.q: What if I ignore a Delaware violation notice?
faqs.a: The city can fix the problem and bill you, and an unpaid bill may become a lien or join your property tax bill. It can also recommend charges through the city prosecutor.

faqs.q: Where is the Delaware County Recorder and what are its deed fees?
faqs.a: The Recorder's office is at 145 N. Union Street in Delaware. Its fee page shows $39 for the first two pages, with a $5 preservation surcharge built in, and $8 per added page.

faqs.q: How do I tell which district my Delaware home is in?
faqs.a: It might be Delaware City, Olentangy Local or Buckeye Valley, since all three reach into the city. Match the parcel with county records or the district before naming one.
